title: Effect of Process Control Agent on the Mechanosynthesis of the Non-Equiatomic High Entropy Alloy Al12Mo10Fe35Mn23Ni20
content: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are distinguished by their unique compositional complexity. They typically consist of five or more principal elements, each with an atomic percentage between 5 and 35%, or exhibit a configurational entropy greater than 12.47 J/molK [1, 2]. This multi-element characteristic often leads to unique microstructures and exceptional properties, making HEAs superior and more attractive than conventional alloys [3, 4].
